expectation: CD15 is a membrane/surface stain on neutrophils and granulocytes, with some epithelial and tumour-cell staining. It should appear as a modest subset of small cells, scattered singly or in clusters, often in stroma, near vessels or in inflamed areas.
observed: A: many discrete small yellow cell-sized spots scattered across the ROIs, with denser clusters in the top ROIs. B and C: compact bright cells of about 10 um, some paired or clustered. C also has a diffuse streak along a tissue strip, which fits epithelial staining. D: bright blobs on dim nuclei.
why: CD15 marks a distinct, sparse population of discrete cell-sized cells in clusters and a tissue strip, with low background haze, as expected for neutrophil/epithelial CD15.
notes: Sparse, cell-sized bright cells and clusters, plus a streak of epithelium-like signal in C. Background is low and the signal does not follow nuclear density. The pattern fits neutrophil CD15.
